question: When were the words " Socialist, Secular and Democratic Republic' added in the Indian Constitution?
solution:
The correct answer is __**In the 42nd amendment in 1976**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The words "**Socialist, Secular, and Democratic Republic**" were added to the **Preamble** of the Indian Constitution by the **42nd amendment** in **1976**.
 
• This amendment is often referred to as the **mini-Constitution** due to the extensive changes it brought about.
 
• The inclusion of these words aimed to emphasize the commitment of the Indian state to socialism, secularism, and democracy.
 
• The **42nd Amendment** was enacted during the Emergency period under the Prime Ministership of **Indira Gandhi**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **42nd Amendment** is one of the most comprehensive amendments to the Indian Constitution.
 
• It also brought changes to several other parts of the Constitution, including the **Directive Principles of State Policy** and the **Fundamental Duties**.
 
• The amendment aimed to reduce the power of the judiciary and increase the power of the Parliament and the central government.
 
• The amendment has been subject to criticism and praise, with some viewing it as an attempt to strengthen the Indian state and others seeing it as a move towards authoritarianism.
